<!-- Generated by hack/docsgen from internal/config/schema.go; do not edit. Run `make docs-gen`. -->

Every settings key of `kudurru.yaml`, generated from the metadata table in
`internal/config/schema.go`, the same table `kudurru config schema` prints and
`GET /api/v1/settings/_schema` serves.

**Where a value comes from.** Each layer overrides the one before it:

1. the built-in default (the Default column);
2. the config file (`--config`, `KUDURRU_CONFIG`, default `/etc/kudurru/kudurru.yaml`);
3. the settings file (`settingsFile` or `KUDURRU_SETTINGS_FILE`) for cluster-scope keys,
   which is where changes made in the UI, with `kudurru settings set` or with
   `PATCH /api/v1/settings` are written; it is watched and hot keys apply at once;
4. the environment: `KUDURRU_<SECTION>__<KEY>`, with `__` for every dot of the path
   (`KUDURRU_LOG__LEVEL=debug`), or `KUDURRU_<SECTION>__<KEY>_FILE` naming a file
   that holds the value. `string[]` values are comma-separated; `list` and `map` keys
   can only be set in a file. A key set from the environment is read-only in
   the UI, and a variable that names no key stops the server at start.

**Scope.** `node` keys belong to one host. `cluster` keys are shared by every
node of a deployment.

**Allowed values.** The bold label is the name the UI shows. The *Allowed*
line lists what a key accepts: a closed set, a range, a format (`ip`,
`cidr` for a CIDR or a single address, `hostport`, `url`, `domain`,
`upstream` for a server in dnsproxy syntax), the object a value names (`ref`)
and the members of list and map values. The config file, the environment and
the API reject anything else with an error naming the key.

**Flags.** *host-only* keys can only be set in the file or the environment
on the host, never through the API or the UI (they name listeners, files and
privileged behaviour). *restart* keys take effect after a restart (in
Kubernetes the chart rolls the pods); every other key is applied while the
server runs. *write-only* keys are never returned by the API.

## node

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="node.name"></a>`node.name` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Node name.** Node identity; defaults to the hostname.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_NODE__NAME` |
| <a id="node.lameduck"></a>`node.lameduck` | `duration` | `2s` | node | **Lameduck drain window.** Drain window after SIGTERM: readiness answers 503 and the health name SERVFAIL for this long before the listeners close (0 disables). The Helm chart also runs kudurru lameduck in preStop.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_NODE__LAMEDUCK` |
| <a id="node.dataDir"></a>`node.dataDir` | `string` | `/var/lib/kudurru` | node | **Data directory.** Directory for state.db, querylog.db, local.db, lists and keys.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_NODE__DATADIR` |

## listeners

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="listeners.dns"></a>`listeners.dns` | `list` | `[{address: "0.0.0.0:53", protocols: [udp, tcp]}]` | node | **DNS listeners.** DNS listeners: address and protocols (udp, tcp).<br>Allowed: items: {address (required): string (format hostport); protocols: list of string (one of udp \| tcp) (default \["udp","tcp"\])}.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: file only. |
| <a id="listeners.dot"></a>`listeners.dot` | `list` | `[]` | node | **DNS-over-TLS listeners.** DNS-over-TLS listeners (RFC 7858, ALPN dot): address and tls {certFile, keyFile}.<br>Allowed: items: {address (required): string (format hostport); tls (required): {certFile (required): string; keyFile (required): string}}.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: file only. |
| <a id="listeners.doh"></a>`listeners.doh` | `list` | `[]` | node | **DNS-over-HTTPS listeners.** DNS-over-HTTPS listeners (RFC 8484, HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1): address, path (default /dns-query) and tls {certFile, keyFile}.<br>Allowed: items: {address (required): string (format hostport); path: string (default /dns-query); tls (required): {certFile (required): string; keyFile (required): string}}.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: file only. |
| <a id="listeners.doq"></a>`listeners.doq` | `list` | `[]` | node | **DNS-over-QUIC listeners.** DNS-over-QUIC listeners (RFC 9250, udp, ALPN doq): address and tls {certFile, keyFile}.<br>Allowed: items: {address (required): string (format hostport); tls (required): {certFile (required): string; keyFile (required): string}}.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: file only. |
| <a id="listeners.doh3"></a>`listeners.doh3` | `list` | `[]` | node | **DNS-over-HTTP/3 listeners.** DNS-over-HTTPS over HTTP/3 listeners (udp, ALPN h3): address, path (default /dns-query) and tls {certFile, keyFile}.<br>Allowed: items: {address (required): string (format hostport); path: string (default /dns-query); tls (required): {certFile (required): string; keyFile (required): string}}.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: file only. |
| <a id="listeners.api.address"></a>`listeners.api.address` | `string` | `0.0.0.0:8080` | node | **API and UI address.** HTTP API and UI listener.<br>Allowed: format hostport.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__API__ADDRESS` |
| <a id="listeners.api.tls.auto"></a>`listeners.api.tls.auto` | `string` | `selfsigned` | node | **API automatic TLS.** TLS for the API listener when no certFile is set: selfsigned (generate a certificate once into &lt;node.dataDir&gt;/keys/) or off (plain HTTP, e.g. behind a TLS-terminating proxy).<br>Allowed: one of selfsigned \| off.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__API__TLS__AUTO` |
| <a id="listeners.api.tls.certFile"></a>`listeners.api.tls.certFile` | `string` | (empty) | node | **API certificate file.** API listener certificate (PEM); takes precedence over tls.auto.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__API__TLS__CERTFILE` |
| <a id="listeners.api.tls.keyFile"></a>`listeners.api.tls.keyFile` | `string` | (empty) | node | **API key file.** Private key for listeners.api.tls.certFile.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__API__TLS__KEYFILE` |
| <a id="listeners.api.pathPrefix"></a>`listeners.api.pathPrefix` | `string` | (empty) | node | **API path prefix.** URL path prefix the API and UI are served under when a reverse proxy mounts kudurru below / (e.g. /kudurru).<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__API__PATHPREFIX` |
| <a id="listeners.api.trustedProxies"></a>`listeners.api.trustedProxies` | `string[]` | `[]` | node | **Trusted reverse proxies.** Reverse proxies (addresses or CIDRs) whose X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto headers the API trusts for the client address and scheme.<br>Allowed: items: string (format cidr).<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__API__TRUSTEDPROXIES` |
| <a id="listeners.ops.address"></a>`listeners.ops.address` | `string` | `0.0.0.0:8081` | node | **Health listener address.** Unauthenticated health listener (/healthz/\*).<br>Allowed: format hostport.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__OPS__ADDRESS` |
| <a id="listeners.metrics.address"></a>`listeners.metrics.address` | `string` | `0.0.0.0:9153` | node | **Metrics listener address.** Prometheus /metrics listener.<br>Allowed: format hostport.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__METRICS__ADDRESS` |
| <a id="listeners.proxyProtocolFrom"></a>`listeners.proxyProtocolFrom` | `string[]` | `[]` | node | **PROXYv2 peers.** Exact peers (CIDRs, normally /32) allowed to send PROXYv2 headers; loopback only when dnsdist shares the network namespace.<br>Allowed: items: string (format cidr).<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__PROXYPROTOCOLFROM` |
| <a id="listeners.proxyProtocolSecretFile"></a>`listeners.proxyProtocolSecretFile` | `string` | (empty) | node | **PROXYv2 secret file.** File holding the PROXYv2 TLV 0xE0 secret shared with the dnsdist supervisor (at least 32 bytes, e.g. openssl rand -hex 32); required when proxyProtocolFrom names a non-loopback peer.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__PROXYPROTOCOLSECRETFILE` |
| <a id="listeners.internal.address"></a>`listeners.internal.address` | `string` | `0.0.0.0:8082` | node | **Node-to-node listener address.** Node-to-node listener (list bodies by digest, /internal/status); always TLS.<br>Allowed: format hostport.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__INTERNAL__ADDRESS` |
| <a id="listeners.internal.tokenFile"></a>`listeners.internal.tokenFile` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Internal token file.** File holding the internal bearer token; empty derives it from the encryption key (KUDURRU\_ENCRYPTION\_KEY) with HKDF.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__INTERNAL__TOKENFILE` |
| <a id="listeners.internal.tls.certFile"></a>`listeners.internal.tls.certFile` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Internal certificate file.** Internal listener certificate (PEM); empty issues one from the CA derived from the encryption key.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__INTERNAL__TLS__CERTFILE` |
| <a id="listeners.internal.tls.keyFile"></a>`listeners.internal.tls.keyFile` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Internal key file.** Private key for listeners.internal.tls.certFile.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__INTERNAL__TLS__KEYFILE` |
| <a id="listeners.internal.tls.caFile"></a>`listeners.internal.tls.caFile` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Internal CA bundle.** CA bundle (PEM) trusted when dialling other nodes; empty trusts the CA derived from the encryption key.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__INTERNAL__TLS__CAFILE` |
| <a id="listeners.internal.tls.serverName"></a>`listeners.internal.tls.serverName` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Internal TLS server name.** Name verified in peers' internal certificates; empty uses the derived certificates' fixed name. Set it to a SAN of tls.certFile.<br>Allowed: format domain.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__INTERNAL__TLS__SERVERNAME` |
| <a id="listeners.blockPage.http"></a>`listeners.blockPage.http` | `string` | `:80` | node | **Block page HTTP address.** Plain-HTTP listener of the block page (blockPage.enabled); empty disables it. Browsers that resolve a blocked name under the blockPage response connect here.<br>Allowed: format hostport.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__BLOCKPAGE__HTTP` |
| <a id="listeners.blockPage.https"></a>`listeners.blockPage.https` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Block page HTTPS address.** Optional HTTPS listener of the block page (e.g. :443). No certificate can be valid for the blocked names, so browsers show a certificate warning there, and HSTS sites cannot be bypassed at all (docs/deploy/blocking-page.md); empty disables it.<br>Allowed: format hostport.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__BLOCKPAGE__HTTPS` |
| <a id="listeners.blockPage.tls.certFile"></a>`listeners.blockPage.tls.certFile` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Block page certificate file.** Certificate (PEM) of listeners.blockPage.https; empty generates a self-signed one into &lt;node.dataDir&gt;/keys/blockpage.crt.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__BLOCKPAGE__TLS__CERTFILE` |
| <a id="listeners.blockPage.tls.keyFile"></a>`listeners.blockPage.tls.keyFile` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Block page key file.** Private key for listeners.blockPage.tls.certFile.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__BLOCKPAGE__TLS__KEYFILE` |
| <a id="listeners.sockets"></a>`listeners.sockets` | `int` | `0` | node | **Sockets per DNS listener.** SO\_REUSEPORT sockets per udp and tcp DNS listener, each with its own read loop (Linux; one elsewhere); 0 means GOMAXPROCS, 1 a single socket.<br>Allowed: at least 0.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LISTENERS__SOCKETS` |

## store

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="store.driver"></a>`store.driver` | `string` | `sqlite` | node | **Store driver.** Store driver: sqlite (state.db under node.dataDir) or kube (CRDs via the apiserver).<br>Allowed: one of sqlite \| kube.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_STORE__DRIVER` |
| <a id="store.kube.startupTimeout"></a>`store.kube.startupTimeout` | `duration` | `15s` | node | **Kubernetes sync timeout.** How long to wait for the apiserver watches to sync before serving from local.db.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_STORE__KUBE__STARTUPTIMEOUT` |
| <a id="store.kube.snapshot.maxAge"></a>`store.kube.snapshot.maxAge` | `duration` | `24h` | node | **Snapshot maximum age.** Oldest local.db snapshot that may still answer primary zones; older snapshots answer SERVFAIL while forwarding continues.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_STORE__KUBE__SNAPSHOT__MAXAGE` |

## upstreams

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="upstreams.groups"></a>`upstreams.groups` | `map` | `{default: {servers: ["1.1.1.1:53", "9.9.9.9:53"], strategy: parallel_best, timeout: 2s}}` | cluster | **Upstream groups.** Named upstream groups: servers, strategy (parallel\_best, strict, random, rtt\_weighted), timeout.<br>Allowed: values: {servers (required): list of string (format upstream); strategy: string (one of parallel\_best \| strict \| random \| rtt\_weighted, default parallel\_best); timeout: duration (default 2s)}.<br>Environment: file only. |
| <a id="upstreams.bootstrap"></a>`upstreams.bootstrap` | `string[]` | `["1.1.1.1:53"]` | cluster | **Bootstrap resolvers.** Plain resolvers used to resolve upstream hostnames (DoT/DoH).<br>Allowed: items: string (format upstream).<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_UPSTREAMS__BOOTSTRAP` |
| <a id="upstreams.conditional"></a>`upstreams.conditional` | `map` | `{}` | cluster | **Conditional forwarding.** Suffix to upstream group map for conditional forwarding (longest suffix wins); a key may list several suffixes in dnsmasq form, "\[/corp.example/10.in-addr.arpa/\]". Conditional answers are never cached.<br>Allowed: values: string (ref upstreamGroup).<br>Environment: file only. |
| <a id="upstreams.ecs.mode"></a>`upstreams.ecs.mode` | `string` | `strip` | cluster | **EDNS Client Subnet.** EDNS Client Subnet on upstream queries: strip (never send one; privacy default), forward (pass the client's own option), add (forward the client's option, else derive one from a public client address).<br>Allowed: one of strip \| forward \| add.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_UPSTREAMS__ECS__MODE` |
| <a id="upstreams.ecs.ipv4Prefix"></a>`upstreams.ecs.ipv4Prefix` | `int` | `24` | cluster | **ECS IPv4 prefix length.** Longest IPv4 source prefix sent upstream in ECS (0-32).<br>Allowed: range 0-32.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_UPSTREAMS__ECS__IPV4PREFIX` |
| <a id="upstreams.ecs.ipv6Prefix"></a>`upstreams.ecs.ipv6Prefix` | `int` | `56` | cluster | **ECS IPv6 prefix length.** Longest IPv6 source prefix sent upstream in ECS (0-128).<br>Allowed: range 0-128.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_UPSTREAMS__ECS__IPV6PREFIX` |

## cache

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="cache.maxEntries"></a>`cache.maxEntries` | `int` | `200000` | cluster | **Maximum cache entries.** Maximum number of cached responses (LRU beyond it); 0 disables the cache.<br>Allowed: at least 0.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_CACHE__MAXENTRIES` |
| <a id="cache.minTTL"></a>`cache.minTTL` | `duration` | `5s` | cluster | **Minimum TTL.** Lower clamp for positive answer TTLs.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_CACHE__MINTTL` |
| <a id="cache.maxTTL"></a>`cache.maxTTL` | `duration` | `24h` | cluster | **Maximum TTL.** Upper clamp for answer TTLs.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_CACHE__MAXTTL` |
| <a id="cache.negativeTTL"></a>`cache.negativeTTL` | `duration` | `5m` | cluster | **Maximum negative TTL.** Upper clamp for NXDOMAIN/NODATA TTLs (RFC 2308 SOA minimum otherwise).<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_CACHE__NEGATIVETTL` |
| <a id="cache.prefetch.threshold"></a>`cache.prefetch.threshold` | `int` | `5` | cluster | **Prefetch threshold (hits).** Hits within prefetch.window that make an entry hot enough to refresh before it expires; 0 disables prefetch.<br>Allowed: at least 0.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_CACHE__PREFETCH__THRESHOLD` |
| <a id="cache.prefetch.window"></a>`cache.prefetch.window` | `duration` | `2h` | cluster | **Prefetch window.** Window over which prefetch hits are counted.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_CACHE__PREFETCH__WINDOW` |
| <a id="cache.serveStale.ttl"></a>`cache.serveStale.ttl` | `duration` | `72h` | cluster | **Serve stale for.** How long past expiry an answer may be served stale when every upstream fails (RFC 8767); 0 disables serve-stale.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_CACHE__SERVESTALE__TTL` |
| <a id="cache.serveStale.answerTTL"></a>`cache.serveStale.answerTTL` | `duration` | `30s` | cluster | **Stale answer TTL.** TTL of stale answers (RFC 8767).<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_CACHE__SERVESTALE__ANSWERTTL` |
| <a id="cache.serveStale.maxWait"></a>`cache.serveStale.maxWait` | `duration` | `1800ms` | cluster | **Stale answer wait.** How long a query for an expired entry waits for the upstream refresh before the stale answer is sent (RFC 8767 client response timer).<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_CACHE__SERVESTALE__MAXWAIT` |

## blocking

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="blocking.enabled"></a>`blocking.enabled` | `bool` | `true` | cluster | **Blocking enabled.** Apply blocklists to recursive queries; false answers everything unfiltered (temporary disable is a runtime toggle, not this key).<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKING__ENABLED` |
| <a id="blocking.defaultResponse"></a>`blocking.defaultResponse` | `string` | `zeroIP` | cluster | **Default block response.** Block response when neither the Policy (blockMode) nor the BlockList (response) sets one: zeroIP (0.0.0.0 / ::, other types NODATA), nxdomain, customIP (blocking.customIP), refused (discouraged: stub resolvers fail over), blockPage (A and AAAA answer the block page address, other types NODATA).<br>Allowed: one of zeroIP \| nxdomain \| customIP \| refused \| blockPage.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKING__DEFAULTRESPONSE` |
| <a id="blocking.blockTTL"></a>`blocking.blockTTL` | `duration` | `10m` | cluster | **Block response TTL.** TTL of block responses when the Policy sets no blockTTL; short so a one-click allow takes effect quickly.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKING__BLOCKTTL` |
| <a id="blocking.allowDegraded"></a>`blocking.allowDegraded` | `bool` | `true` | cluster | **Serve while lists load.** Report ready and serve while referenced blocklists are not loaded yet (queries are filtered by the lists that are loaded).<br>*restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKING__ALLOWDEGRADED` |
| <a id="blocking.customIP.v4"></a>`blocking.customIP.v4` | `string` | (empty) | cluster | **Custom block IPv4.** IPv4 answer for blocked A queries when the response is customIP; empty answers NODATA.<br>Allowed: format ipv4.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKING__CUSTOMIP__V4` |
| <a id="blocking.customIP.v6"></a>`blocking.customIP.v6` | `string` | (empty) | cluster | **Custom block IPv6.** IPv6 answer for blocked AAAA queries when the response is customIP; empty answers NODATA.<br>Allowed: format ipv6.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKING__CUSTOMIP__V6` |
| <a id="blocking.refreshInterval"></a>`blocking.refreshInterval` | `duration` | `24h` | cluster | **List refresh interval.** Refresh interval of BlockLists that set no spec.refreshInterval (at least 1m); the leader fetches, replicas pull by digest.<br>*restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKING__REFRESHINTERVAL` |
| <a id="blocking.initStrategy"></a>`blocking.initStrategy` | `string` | `fast` | cluster | **List loading at start.** Blocklist loading at start: fast (serve at once from the disk cache, load in the background), blocking (not ready until every list is loaded), failOnError (blocking, and exit when a list fails to load).<br>Allowed: one of fast \| blocking \| failOnError.<br>*restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKING__INITSTRATEGY` |
| <a id="blocking.listsDir"></a>`blocking.listsDir` | `string` | (empty) | node | **List cache directory.** Blocklist body cache (sha256(url) files); empty means &lt;node.dataDir&gt;/lists.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKING__LISTSDIR` |
| <a id="blocking.allowLocalListURLs"></a>`blocking.allowLocalListURLs` | `bool` | `false` | node | **Allow local list URLs.** Let BlockList URLs reach loopback, link-local (169.254.0.0/16, fe80::/10: cloud metadata), unspecified and multicast addresses. Off by default so a BlockList writer cannot make the node fetch its own or the cloud's internal services (SSRF); private LAN ranges are always allowed.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKING__ALLOWLOCALLISTURLS` |
| <a id="blocking.catalogue.url"></a>`blocking.catalogue.url` | `string` | (empty) | cluster | **Catalogue URL.** URL of a blocked-services and safe-search catalogue document (schema version 1, docs/deploy/blocked-services.md) that replaces the embedded one; empty serves the catalogue built into the binary. The leader downloads it, replicas pull the leader's copy; a document that fails validation keeps the catalogue in service.<br>Allowed: format url.<br>*restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKING__CATALOGUE__URL` |
| <a id="blocking.catalogue.refreshInterval"></a>`blocking.catalogue.refreshInterval` | `duration` | `24h` | cluster | **Catalogue refresh interval.** How often the leader downloads blocking.catalogue.url (at least 1m; conditional GET).<br>*restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKING__CATALOGUE__REFRESHINTERVAL` |

## blockPage

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="blockPage.enabled"></a>`blockPage.enabled` | `bool` | `false` | cluster | **Block page enabled.** Serve the block page on listeners.blockPage and allow the blockPage block response, which answers blocked A/AAAA queries with blockPage.ipv4/ipv6 (other types NODATA) so browsers show a page explaining the block.<br>*restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKPAGE__ENABLED` |
| <a id="blockPage.ipv4"></a>`blockPage.ipv4` | `string` | (empty) | cluster | **Block page IPv4 address.** IPv4 address blocked A queries are answered with under the blockPage response: this node's address, or a VIP or load balancer in front of the block page. Empty uses the first specific address of listeners.blockPage, else of listeners.dns; with neither, blockPage.enabled is refused.<br>Allowed: format ipv4.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKPAGE__IPV4` |
| <a id="blockPage.ipv6"></a>`blockPage.ipv6` | `string` | (empty) | cluster | **Block page IPv6 address.** IPv6 address blocked AAAA queries are answered with under the blockPage response; empty derives it like blockPage.ipv4, and without one AAAA queries get NODATA.<br>Allowed: format ipv6.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKPAGE__IPV6` |
| <a id="blockPage.title"></a>`blockPage.title` | `string` | `This site is blocked` | cluster | **Page title.** Heading of the block page (plain text, at most 200 characters).<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKPAGE__TITLE` |
| <a id="blockPage.message"></a>`blockPage.message` | `string` | `The administrator of this network has blocked access to this domain.` | cluster | **Page message.** Explanation under the heading (plain text, at most 2000 characters; HTML is shown as text).<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKPAGE__MESSAGE` |
| <a id="blockPage.contact"></a>`blockPage.contact` | `string` | (empty) | cluster | **Administrator contact.** Administrator contact shown as "Ask your administrator": an email address or an http(s) URL; empty omits the line.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKPAGE__CONTACT` |
| <a id="blockPage.showDetails"></a>`blockPage.showDetails` | `bool` | `true` | cluster | **Show block details.** Show the client what blocked the name (list, rule, blocked service, safe search, policy), looked up in the recent query log; false shows only the domain, client, node and time.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKPAGE__SHOWDETAILS` |
| <a id="blockPage.dashboardURL"></a>`blockPage.dashboardURL` | `string` | (empty) | cluster | **Dashboard URL.** Dashboard URL the block page links administrators to (&lt;url&gt;/queries?domain=...); empty derives it from the block page address and listeners.api.<br>Allowed: format url.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKPAGE__DASHBOARDURL` |
| <a id="blockPage.rateLimit"></a>`blockPage.rateLimit` | `int` | `120` | cluster | **Requests per minute per client.** Block page requests per minute per client address (bursts up to the same number); over the limit the listener answers 429. 0 disables the limit.<br>Allowed: range 0-100000.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_BLOCKPAGE__RATELIMIT` |

## querylog

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="querylog.enabled"></a>`querylog.enabled` | `bool` | `true` | cluster | **Query log enabled.** Collect the per-node query log (querylog.db, rollups and the stats API).<br>*restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_QUERYLOG__ENABLED` |
| <a id="querylog.sink"></a>`querylog.sink` | `string` | `sqlite` | cluster | **Query log sink.** Built-in query-log sink: sqlite (querylog.db with rollups; required for the dashboard) or slog (one JSON log line per query, nothing stored).<br>Allowed: one of sqlite \| slog.<br>*restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_QUERYLOG__SINK` |
| <a id="querylog.privacy"></a>`querylog.privacy` | `string` | `full` | cluster | **Query log privacy.** Privacy applied once at ingest, irreversibly: full, anonymize\_client, hide\_domains, hide\_domains\_clients or nothing (per-minute totals only). The answer summary is stored only in full.<br>Allowed: one of full \| anonymize\_client \| hide\_domains \| hide\_domains\_clients \| nothing.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_QUERYLOG__PRIVACY` |
| <a id="querylog.anonymize"></a>`querylog.anonymize` | `string` | `prefix` | cluster | **Client anonymization.** How anonymize\_client hides clients: prefix (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /48) or pseudonym (HMAC with a random in-memory key rotated daily; stable for a day, not reversible).<br>Allowed: one of prefix \| pseudonym.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_QUERYLOG__ANONYMIZE` |
| <a id="querylog.retention.raw"></a>`querylog.retention.raw` | `duration` | `720h` | cluster | **Keep query rows for.** How long per-query rows are kept (rollups: 35 d per minute, 400 d per hour, daily forever); 0 keeps rows until maxDBBytes is reached.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_QUERYLOG__RETENTION__RAW` |
| <a id="querylog.retention.maxDBBytes"></a>`querylog.retention.maxDBBytes` | `bytes` | `10GiB` | cluster | **Maximum query log size.** Upper bound for querylog.db; the oldest rows are deleted first when it is exceeded. 0 disables the cap.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_QUERYLOG__RETENTION__MAXDBBYTES` |
| <a id="querylog.exclude.domains"></a>`querylog.exclude.domains` | `string[]` | `[]` | cluster | **Domains never logged.** Names never logged: exact names, \*.suffix wildcards (the suffix and everything below it) or /regex/.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_QUERYLOG__EXCLUDE__DOMAINS` |
| <a id="querylog.exclude.clients"></a>`querylog.exclude.clients` | `string[]` | `[]` | cluster | **Clients never logged.** Clients never logged: IP addresses, CIDR prefixes or client names.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_QUERYLOG__EXCLUDE__CLIENTS` |
| <a id="querylog.exclude.sudn"></a>`querylog.exclude.sudn` | `bool` | `true` | cluster | **Skip special-use names.** Do not log special-use names (localhost, .local, .home.arpa, private and link-local reverse zones).<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_QUERYLOG__EXCLUDE__SUDN` |

## ratelimit

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="ratelimit.enabled"></a>`ratelimit.enabled` | `bool` | `true` | cluster | **Rate limiting enabled.** Per-prefix QPM rate limiting of UDP queries at ingress; TCP, DoT, DoH, DoQ and DoH3 are never limited, nor loopback clients and the health name.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_RATELIMIT__ENABLED` |
| <a id="ratelimit.ipv4"></a>`ratelimit.ipv4` | `map` | `{24: 6000, 32: 600}` | cluster | **IPv4 limits (queries per minute).** IPv4 prefix length to queries per minute per prefix (token bucket holding one minute's allowance); merged with the defaults key by key, 0 disables a level.<br>Allowed: keys: int (range 0-32); values: int (at least 0).<br>Environment: file only. |
| <a id="ratelimit.ipv6"></a>`ratelimit.ipv6` | `map` | `{128: 600, 56: 12000, 64: 6000}` | cluster | **IPv6 limits (queries per minute).** IPv6 prefix length to queries per minute per prefix; merged with the defaults key by key, 0 disables a level.<br>Allowed: keys: int (range 0-128); values: int (at least 0).<br>Environment: file only. |
| <a id="ratelimit.slip"></a>`ratelimit.slip` | `int` | `50` | cluster | **Slip (percent answered TC=1).** Percentage (0-100) of over-limit UDP queries answered with an empty TC=1 response so real clients retry over TCP; the rest are dropped.<br>Allowed: range 0-100.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_RATELIMIT__SLIP` |
| <a id="ratelimit.maxBuckets"></a>`ratelimit.maxBuckets` | `int` | `65536` | cluster | **Tracked prefixes.** Most prefixes tracked at once (LRU); an evicted prefix starts with a full bucket.<br>Allowed: at least 0.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_RATELIMIT__MAXBUCKETS` |
| <a id="ratelimit.exempt"></a>`ratelimit.exempt` | `string[]` | `[]` | cluster | **Exempt clients.** CIDRs or addresses never rate limited (loopback always is).<br>Allowed: items: string (format cidr).<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_RATELIMIT__EXEMPT` |

## Top-level keys

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="objects"></a>`objects` | `list` | `[]` | node | **Inline objects.** Inline CRD-shaped objects (zones, lists, groups, policies); file-managed as file:kudurru.yaml and re-applied on start.<br>Allowed: items: {apiVersion: string; kind: string; metadata: object; spec: object}.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: file only. |
| <a id="settingsFile"></a>`settingsFile` | `string` | (empty) | node | **Settings file.** Settings file layered over this file for the cluster-scope keys and watched for changes (hot reload, D25); KUDURRU\_SETTINGS\_FILE takes precedence. The Helm chart mounts /etc/kudurru/settings/settings.yaml; in Docker PATCH /api/v1/settings persists into it. Empty disables the layer.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_SETTINGSFILE` |
| <a id="objectsDir"></a>`objectsDir` | `string` | `/etc/kudurru/objects.d` | node | **Objects directory.** Directory of \*.yaml object files, file-managed as file:&lt;dir&gt;/&lt;name&gt; and re-applied on change; deleting a document deletes the object.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_OBJECTSDIR` |
| <a id="tsigKeys"></a>`tsigKeys` | `list` |  | node | **TSIG keys.** TSIG keys (RFC 8945) for zone transfers and NOTIFY: name (referenced by DNSZone spec.policy.transferTSIGKeyRefs), algorithm (hmac-sha256, hmac-sha512) and secretFile holding the base64 secret (tsig-keygen format).<br>Allowed: items: {name (required): string (format domain); algorithm (required): string (one of hmac-sha256 \| hmac-sha512); secretFile (required): string}.<br>*host-only, restart, write-only*<br>Environment: file only. |

## notify

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="notify.source"></a>`notify.source` | `string` | (empty) | node | **NOTIFY source address.** Local IP address outbound NOTIFY messages are sent from; empty lets the kernel choose. Secondaries must list it as a primary.<br>Allowed: format ip.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_NOTIFY__SOURCE` |

## externalDNS

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="externalDNS.webhook.enabled"></a>`externalDNS.webhook.enabled` | `bool` | `false` | node | **external-dns webhook enabled.** Serve the external-dns webhook provider (GET /, GET/POST /records, POST /adjustendpoints) on externalDNS.webhook.listen.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_EXTERNALDNS__WEBHOOK__ENABLED` |
| <a id="externalDNS.webhook.listen"></a>`externalDNS.webhook.listen` | `string` | `127.0.0.1:8888` | node | **external-dns webhook address.** Listener of the external-dns webhook. It has no authentication, so the default is loopback (external-dns as a sidecar or on the same host); a wider address (the chart renders :&lt;port&gt; behind its NetworkPolicy) lets every client that reaches it write records.<br>Allowed: format hostport.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_EXTERNALDNS__WEBHOOK__LISTEN` |
| <a id="externalDNS.webhook.namespace"></a>`externalDNS.webhook.namespace` | `string` | `external-dns` | node | **external-dns record namespace.** Namespace of the DNSRecordSets the webhook writes (managed by integration:external-dns, one record set per DNS name).<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_EXTERNALDNS__WEBHOOK__NAMESPACE` |
| <a id="externalDNS.webhook.zoneSelector"></a>`externalDNS.webhook.zoneSelector` | `map` | `{}` | node | **external-dns zone selector.** Label selector (key: value) choosing the primary DNSZones external-dns may write to; empty allows every primary zone.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: file only. |

## auth

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="auth.localLogin"></a>`auth.localLogin` | `string` | `enabled` | cluster | **Local password login.** Local password login (POST /api/v1/auth/login): enabled, admins-only (builtin admins only) or disabled; `kudurru admin` over the admin socket always works.<br>Allowed: one of enabled \| admins-only \| disabled.<br>*restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_AUTH__LOCALLOGIN` |
| <a id="auth.bootstrap.adminPasswordFile"></a>`auth.bootstrap.adminPasswordFile` | `string` | (empty) | node | **First-boot admin password file.** File holding the first-boot admin password; KUDURRU\_ADMIN\_PASSWORD\[\_FILE\] take precedence, and without either a password is generated and printed once.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_AUTH__BOOTSTRAP__ADMINPASSWORDFILE` |
| <a id="auth.session.idleTimeout"></a>`auth.session.idleTimeout` | `duration` | `30m` | cluster | **Session idle timeout.** Sliding idle timeout of a UI session (at least 1m).<br>*restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_AUTH__SESSION__IDLETIMEOUT` |
| <a id="auth.session.lifetime"></a>`auth.session.lifetime` | `duration` | `12h` | cluster | **Session lifetime.** Absolute lifetime of a UI session; roles are re-resolved at the next login.<br>*restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_AUTH__SESSION__LIFETIME` |
| <a id="auth.session.secure"></a>`auth.session.secure` | `string` | `auto` | cluster | **Secure session cookie.** Session cookie Secure attribute: auto (when TLS terminates here or a trusted proxy reports https), always or never.<br>Allowed: one of auto \| always \| never.<br>*restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_AUTH__SESSION__SECURE` |
| <a id="auth.tokens.maxLifetime"></a>`auth.tokens.maxLifetime` | `duration` | `0s` | cluster | **Maximum token lifetime.** Longest lifetime of a new API token; tokens without expiry get it. 0 allows tokens that never expire.<br>*restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_AUTH__TOKENS__MAXLIFETIME` |
| <a id="auth.identityProviders"></a>`auth.identityProviders` | `list` | `[]` | cluster | **Identity providers.** OpenID Providers for UI login and bearer ID tokens: id, issuer, clientID, clientSecretFile, redirectURL, cliClientID, scopes, claimValidationRules, claimMappings, provisioning.<br>Allowed: items: {id (required): string; displayName: string; issuer: string (format url); clientID: string; clientSecretFile: string; cliClientID: string; redirectURL: string (format url); scopes: list of string; audiences: list of string; claimValidationRules: list of object; claimMappings: object; provisioning: object; allowedDomains: list of string (format domain)}.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: file only. |
| <a id="auth.kubernetes.mode"></a>`auth.kubernetes.mode` | `string` | `sar` | cluster | **Kubernetes authorization.** How Kubernetes service-account tokens are authorized: sar (SubjectAccessReview on kudurru.io resources). impersonate is v0.2.<br>Allowed: one of sar.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_AUTH__KUBERNETES__MODE` |
| <a id="auth.adminSocket.path"></a>`auth.adminSocket.path` | `string` | `/run/kudurru/kudurru.sock` | node | **Admin socket path.** Unix socket for `kudurru admin` (reset-password, create-token, list-users); peers must be uid 0, the server's uid or in adminSocket.group. Empty disables it.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_AUTH__ADMINSOCKET__PATH` |
| <a id="auth.adminSocket.group"></a>`auth.adminSocket.group` | `int` | `-1` | node | **Admin socket group (gid).** Extra gid allowed on the admin socket; -1 for none.<br>Allowed: at least -1.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_AUTH__ADMINSOCKET__GROUP` |

## rbac

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="rbac.bindings"></a>`rbac.bindings` | `list` | `[]` | cluster | **Role bindings.** Role bindings: role, scope {kind cluster\|zone, name} and subjects \[{kind User\|Group\|ServiceAccount, name, namespace}\]; RoleBinding objects add to them.<br>Allowed: items: {role (required): string (one of viewer \| auditor \| operator \| zone-admin \| admin); scope: {kind: string (one of cluster \| zone \| zonegroup \| clientgroup, default cluster); name: string}; subjects (required): list of {kind (required): string (one of User \| Group \| ServiceAccount); name (required): string; namespace: string}}.<br>*host-only, restart*<br>Environment: file only. |

## log

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="log.level"></a>`log.level` | `string` | `info` | node | **Log level.** Log level: debug, info, warn, error. Per-role overrides as info,dns=debug.<br>Allowed: one of debug \| info \| warn \| error.<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LOG__LEVEL` |
| <a id="log.format"></a>`log.format` | `string` | `json` | node | **Log format.** Log format: json or text.<br>Allowed: one of json \| text.<br>*restart*<br>Environment: `KUDURRU_LOG__FORMAT` |
